Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Elena Vasquez, CEO; Marcus Hale, CFO; Dr. Lena Kim, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Sofia Chen, Chief Supply Chain Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q2 2024 marked a transformative period for Voltara Motors, underscoring our leadership in the EV transition amid a rapidly evolving global automotive landscape. We delivered record quarterly revenue of $2.8 billion, a robust 48% year-over-year increase, surpassing our guidance by a wide margin. This was powered by a 52% surge in vehicle deliveries to 65,000 units globally, ahead of our target range, with our core EV lineup including the Apex sedan and Summit SUV driving the momentum. The newly launched Apex Pro variant, our premium long-range model with 520 miles of EPA-estimated range, ramped to strong uptake, capturing meaningful share in the U.S. mid-premium segment.

Gross profit reflected class-leading automotive gross margins of 18.2%, up significantly from prior periods, thanks to vertical integration like our next-gen 4680 cylindrical cells at Gigafactory Nevada supplying a growing portion of packs. Cell costs dropped sharply, putting us ahead of peers on the path to sub-$60 per kWh. Adjusted EBITDA was positive, and free cash flow turned constructive, bolstering our liquidity to over $4.5 billion. Production scalability shone through, with Fremont and Berlin Gigafactories approaching high utilization via unibody gigacasting across most of our lineup, cutting body-in-white costs dramatically. We domesticated much of our battery materials under the IRA, qualifying for substantial tax credits that flowed to a large share of U.S. deliveries.

Regionally, North America was our stronghold with strong growth fueled by IRA tailwinds and demand for the Summit SUV, outselling key competitors. Europe exploded with triple-digit growth, gaining market share despite headwinds, shielded by localization at Berlin from Chinese tariffs. In China, our Shanghai JV ramped impressively amid local challenges. Innovation accelerated our moat: we advanced our Voltara Autonomy Platform to new certifications with massive fleet data training, powering advanced features on major routes. Battery prototypes hit impressive densities, and sustainability metrics improved sharply, earning index recognition.

Our order backlog grew substantially to provide strong visibility, weighted to high-margin trims. These results validate our scale-smart approach: cost discipline through innovations paired with capacity growth. We're on pace for robust full-year growth and raising long-term targets.

As we look ahead to Q3 2024 and full-year 2025, our priorities are laser-focused on scaling sustainable profitability as global EV penetration climbs toward 22%, driven by falling battery costs around $85 per kWh and policies like the U.S. IRA's $7,500 credit. First, accelerating production ramp and vertical integration: ramping Nevada Gigafactory 2 to 100,000 units annualized by quarter-end, leveraging in-house 4680 cells that cut pack costs 22% quarter-over-quarter. We'll reach 60 GWh cell output by end-2025, feeding the Apex SUV and new Boltstream sedan in H2, prioritizing LFP for 40% of packs from our South Carolina cathode plant to slash cobalt dependency 70% and improve cold-weather performance versus rivals.

For FY2025, we target 450,000 deliveries, up 143%, with ASP steady at $48,000 via mix-shift to higher-margin models. Capex peaks at $3.2 billion for a third U.S. Gigafactory in Georgia, but positive free cash flow of $800 million by Q4. Second, advancing autonomy and software: rolling out Voltara Autonomy 3.0, Level 3 hands-free standard on Apex, with 5 million supervised miles. By year-end, OTA updates for V2G charging unlock $500 million recurring revenue at 85% margins, investing $450 million in AI compute with NVIDIA partners to cut neural net loop times.

Third, regional expansion: North America at 65% volume, defending #3 U.S. share with 50,000 Boltstream units at $35,000 MSRP, IRA-eligible, plus leasing to counter high rates. Europe 20%, localizing 80% post-Berlin JV with VW for a 300-mile LFP hatchback, targeting 8% Germany/UK share. China/APAC 10%, doubling Shanghai SKD with 800V fast-charging. Emerging markets 5%, piloting sodium-ion with Tata in India/Mexico.

Fourth, supply chain resilience: 60% hedged on lithium amid $12,000/tonne spikes, 30% recycled content cutting COGS 8%, expanding auto margins to 24%. ESG: 50% renewables by Q3. Fifth, capital allocation: $500 million share repurchases, potential dividend in 2026, M&A in charging, targeting $15 billion revenue.

In summary, execution on scale, software, and sustainability for 30%+ ROIC in a $1 trillion TAM.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. Good morning, everyone. For Q2 2024, our revenue was $2.8 billion, representing a substantial 48% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin reached 18.2%, driven by production efficiencies, favorable mix, and cost reductions. Operating expenses were controlled at $650 million, and net income was $180 million. We ended with $4.5 billion in cash reserves. We project Q3 revenue of $3.2 to $3.5 billion and continued margin expansion.

Diving deeper into key financial aspects, let's start with average selling price trends by model and region, a critical lever for profitability amid competitive pressures from Tesla, BYD, Ford, and Volkswagen, plus our cost-down efforts. Our global blended ASP was $58,200, up 7% YoY from $54,400 and 2% QoQ from $57,000, beating guidance due to mix toward higher-margin Summit SUV and Apex sedan, plus strong software uptake on our Full Autonomy Suite—adding $4,500 per vehicle on average. Entry-level Spark in China faced some pressure from price wars.

By model: Apex flagship sedan ASP steady at $96,800, up 4% YoY, with 68% Long Range Dual Motor AWD at $102k+ and 52% FAS penetration, up from 41%, bolstered by 800V architecture for 10-80% charging in under 18 minutes and fleet demand like Waymo trends. Summit mid-size SUV, our volume leader, hit $67,500, up 12% YoY, with performance trim take-rates at 45% via Hawk Eye ADAS with LiDAR; in-house 4680 cells at $85/kWh LFP equivalent allowed a $1,500 base cut against Tesla Model Y. Titan full-size pickup at $84,200, flat YoY but up 3% QoQ, with towing to 14,000 lbs and Tri-Motor at $110k, $7,500 incentives like Rivian R1T, but 61% FAS at $5,800 uplift. Spark compact hatch dipped to $39,800, down 3% YoY, chasing volume against BYD Seagull, but structural packs preserved 22% margins. Net, Summit/Apex at 62% volumes drove $3,800 blended uplift.

By region: North America, 42% volumes, $64,500 ASP up 9% YoY, IRA $7,500 credits on 85% US-made units, California ZEV $1,200 tailwind, fleet discounts down to 8%. Europe, 28%, $59,800 up 6%, Apex demand in Germany/UK shielded by 38% EU tariffs on Chinese imports, Berlin output with €4,000 subsidies. China/APAC 25%, $44,200 down 2%, $2,000 adjustments vs. NIO/Xiaomi, but CATL Qilin at $62/kWh for 18% margins, 95% localization, 35% FAS subs. Rest of World 5%, $52,000 flat, Summit exports to Australia/Middle East.

For Q3, blended ASP $59,000-$60,500, 3-5% QoQ growth from 4680 scale to 50 GWh targeting $70/kWh, 65% premium mix, FAS v12 at $6,000, regional subsidies, dynamic pricing, $250 million H2 credits. This resilience highlights premium positioning.

Shifting to battery costs per kWh, pivotal as packs are 30-40% of BOM. Q2 pack average was $92/kWh, down 12% YoY from $105 and 38% from $148 in 2020. Cell-level $68/kWh NMC 811, nearing sub-$60 target, top quartile vs. Tesla $70-75, LG $80-90. BloombergNEF global at $139/kWh 2023 down 14%; we outpace via Nevada 80 GWh capacity. Trends: LFP 45% volume up from 25%, CATL Qilin $55/kWh, 205 Wh/kg for $4,500 savings on entry SUV. Dry electrode cuts solvents 30%, 4x throughput, 95% OEE; cell-to-pack saves 15%. Materials: CAM down 25% QoQ, graphite $5-6/kWh, silicon-doped pilots. Recycling with Redwood $3-5/kWh credit.

Regional: China $45-55/kWh CATL/BYD, tariffs mitigated by JV; NA $85/kWh LGES/SK with IRA $45/kWh; Europe $100+ Northvolt; Korea/Japan $75-85. Initiatives: 4680 25% Q3 output, tabless 16% range uplift; solid-state $250M capex 400 Wh/kg; Anovion graphite acquire; 70% lithium hedge $12k/tonne. Guide $82/kWh FY2024 down 18%, $65/kWh 2026. This flywheel enables 25% margins on $35k models.

On order backlog and reservations: Global backlog $18.7 billion, 285,000 units at $65,600 ASP, up 22% YoY, 8% QoQ. Reservations 420,000 at $62,200 ASP, up 18% YoY. V-Truck 42% at $7.9B/112k units up 28% YoY; V-Summit SUV 35% $6.5B/92k, reservations +25%; V-Stream sedan 18% $3.4B/52k down 5% YoY but 65% conversions. NA 58% $10.9B up 25%, IRA/Texas ramp; Europe 24% $4.5B +30%, Berlin 250k run-rate; APAC 12% $2.2B dip but +40% reservations post-LFP; emerging 6%.

Drivers: 78% FAS take-rate $12k uplift, price stability 28% gross, backlog 14 months visibility. Q3 to $20B+ with Nevada Phase 2, 55-60% conversions, $1.2B FCF run-rate.

Gross margin per vehicle was $15,420, up 19.5% YoY from $12,910, 4.2% QoQ from $14,800, on track for $15,000 FY average ahead of $13,500 guide. Outperforms Tesla ~$13,800, Rivian sub-$10k. ASP $52,300 up 7.8% YoY, CyberHaul double QoQ $68k, AeroSedan 2.0 $45k, 15% FAS $8-12k. COGS $36,880 down 12.3% YoY, 46-series $112/kWh down 28%, silicon-anode 320 Wh/kg cobalt -80%, structural packs -$1,200. OEE 92%, megacasting 70% SKU -400, $285M credits $1,100/vehicle.

NA $17,200 23% margin IRA $7,500; Europe $14,500 20%; China $12,800 15% localizing. Q4 $16,500-$17,000 CyberHaul 25k, GigaMexico, 25% FAS. Vertical 85% in-house flywheel to $20k+ 2027.

For gross margin guidance: Q2 non-GAAP auto 18.2%, up sharply. Q3 20-22%, FY2025 18-20% on 220-250k deliveries. Assumptions: Q3 70-75k deliveries 20% up, Apex 70% mix, CPV $44-45k down 12-15%, utilization 85%. ASP $54-56k flat, credits 1.5-2pts. Variables: batteries $105/kWh down 18% YoY LFP/CATL, dry electrode 8% pack cut, gigacasting $300/unit, warranty 1.8%. NA 75% IRA $7,500; Europe 20% flat 12k; China 5% 8-10%. FX 1.08 USD/EUR 7.25 CNY, 70% LCE hedge. Inflection to profitability like Tesla Model Y.

We're in a strong financial position. Next, Dr. Lena Kim will share updates on manufacturing.

Dr. Lena Kim:
Thank you, Marcus. We made significant investments in facilities like Nevada and Berlin to boost capacity and efficiency, achieving record volumes with gigacasting deployed across 85% of lineup, slashing costs 35% versus stamped steel. OEE exceeds 92%, unibody processes mirror and exceed Tesla efficiencies, ramping to 1.2 million annualized run-rate. Domesticating 78% battery materials under IRA, structural packs reduce weight 15%, enabling 520-mile ranges. These efforts cut manufacturing costs per unit sharply while scaling for 450,000 FY2025 deliveries.

After me, Raj Patel on technological advancements.

Raj Patel:
Thank you. Our R&D pushes boundaries in battery tech, autonomy, and connectivity. Voltara Autonomy 3.0 with Level 3 certification on 12 billion miles data for unsupervised highway on 75% routes, OTA V2G, neural nets to 50ms loop. Solid-state at 450 Wh/kg lab, 4680 tabless 16% range uplift, silicon anodes. We're shaping mobility future with software moat, 25% attach, $500M recurring at 85% margins.

Following Raj, Sofia Chen on supply chain.

Sofia Chen:
Thank you. We've built robust strategies to mitigate risks, diversifying with 60% lithium hedges, 30% Redwood recycled content cutting COGS 8%, 95% localization Shanghai/Berlin. Multi-chem LFP/NMC/sodium-ion, partnerships CATL/Panasonic/Verkor, navigating tariffs/geopolitics for resilient material flow. ESG renewables to 50%, aligning sustainability.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one.

Analyst 1:
Hi, thanks for taking my question. On ASP trends, can you elaborate on risks to your Q3 guidance from potential Tesla Robotaxi announcements or EU-China trade issues?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks for the question. Our Q3 ASP guide of $59,000 to $60,500 factors in those risks conservatively. Tesla events could pressure sentiment, but our premium mix 65% Apex/Summit/Titan and FAS v12 at $6,000 provide buffer. EU escalation might hit, but Berlin localization and subsidies shield; we're using dynamic pricing and $250M credits as mitigants. Confident in 3-5% growth.

Analyst 2:
Great, and for gross margin guidance, how sensitive is it to lithium volatility or delivery downside?

Marcus Hale:
Solid question. We've stress-tested: 10% delivery miss still yields 19% Q3 margins. Lithium upside to $18k/tonne hits CPV $1,200, but 70% hedged through Q2 2025 at $15k, plus LFP 45% mix buffers. Volume leverage at 85% utilization drives most expansion; NA IRA and Texas online underpin core 18-20% FY2025.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Dr. Kim, on manufacturing, what's the latest on Nevada ramp and gigacasting yields?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Nevada Gigafactory 2 on track for 100k annualized Q1 2025, 4680 at 92% yields, full 60 GWh by year-end. Gigacasting at 9,000-ton press covers 70% SUV underbody, SKU to 400, OEE 95%, cost savings $300/unit already flowing, scaling fixed costs for 24% margins.

Analyst 4:
Raj, autonomy progress—any updates on Level 4 timeline or NVIDIA partnership details?

Raj Patel:
Level 4 urban by 2026 with $450M AI compute, NVIDIA clusters cutting loops to 50ms on 5M supervised miles. Autonomy 3.0 standard Apex Q1, 25% uptake; V2G OTA partnerships PG&E for grid revenue. Builds consumer scale edge over Waymo.

Analyst 5:
Sofia, supply chain—how are you addressing graphite shortages and nickel bans?

Sofia Chen:
Graphite China-dominant, but Anovion 51% stake locks $4/kWh anodes; Indonesia nickel via long-term offtakes, 95% recycling Redwood. Multi-region: CATL China LFP $55/kWh, LG NA $85 IRA-credited, Verkor Europe sodium pilots $50/kWh 2026. 60% hedges de-risk.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Analyst 6:
Final one: backlog trends strong, but any conversion slowdown from rates? And battery cost outlook?

Elena Vasquez:
Backlog $18.7B gives 14 months visibility, 55-60% H2 conversions despite 7.5% rates slowing sub-$50k 12%; FAS 78% and price stability help. Batteries to $82/kWh FY down 18%, $65 2026 via 4680 scale, dry electrode, solid-state prototypes—unlocks margin machine.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Elena Vasquez for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are well-positioned to capitalize on growing EV demand and deliver strong results through execution on our priorities. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q2 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
